absent: Writer-side per-CPU semaphore acquisition, release and block-counter protocol.
Full layout of percpu_rw_semaphore, its synchronizer and per-CPU counter fields.
Behavior of refcount_warn_saturate and any recovery from saturated state.
Real-time mutex blocking, wakeup, unlock and priority handling.
Task structure and waiter-tree node layout.
Architecture-specific rwlock primitives beyond uniprocessor stubs and contention policy.
Dependence-tracking helpers for rwlock, rwsem and lock class initialization.
Bottom-half enable and interrupt restore ordering beyond these wrappers.

findings.text: Per-CPU reader-writer semaphore exposes shared acquisition and release for readers, with a blocking acquire, a freezable variant honoring a caller flag, a nonblocking try variant reporting success, a matching release, and a predicate testing whether writers have blocked readers.

Reader fast path applies only while the associated synchronizer reports idle, adjusting a per-CPU counter with preemption held off and participating in dependence tracking; when not idle the work delegates to slow helpers with barrier semantics, the try form records dependence only on success, and release mirrors the same idle test.

The per-CPU semaphore interface provides scoped guard helpers for read and write ownership with a conditional try form, a one-shot initializer binding a static lock class, predicates and assertions for held and write-held state, and explicit acquire and release hooks for dependence tracking.
Reference count object is a single-member structure wrapping a signed atomic counter, exposed under a typedef name for use by all refcount helpers.

Maximum usable count equals INT_MAX, saturated error value equals INT_MIN divided by two, initializer sets the inner atomic to a caller supplied value, and a five-member enumeration distinguishes add-not-zero overflow, add overflow, add use-after-free, subtract use-after-free, and decrement leak.

Count raising operations include unconditional set with plain and release ordering, read returning an unsigned view, add-not-zero with relaxed and acquire forms plus a bounded form enforcing a caller limit, and plain add and increment shorthands; conditional forms report the prior value and fail on zero while unconditional forms return no status.

Count lowering operations provide subtract-and-test and decrement-and-test predicates that succeed only when a positive count reaches zero, plus a plain decrement without result, each optionally capturing the prior value for the caller.

Negative or wrapped prior or result values are treated as saturated and trigger a warning helper with a category tag; adding to zero is reported as use-after-free, subtracting past zero or decrementing at or below one is reported as misuse, and reaching zero through subtract inserts acquire ordering after the control dependency.

Callers must not raise a zero count except through conditional helpers, must not drive the counter negative or past the maximum, and must not release a count already at zero or without ownership; all such patterns invoke saturation warnings and leave the object in a saturated error condition rather than a usable count.

Real-time mutex base holds a raw spin wait lock, a cached red-black tree of waiters and an owner pointer, with waiters and owner guarded by the wait lock; the outer mutex embeds the base and optionally a dependence map, initialized with an unlocked wait lock, empty waiter tree and null owner.

Ownership is null when unlocked and otherwise holds a task pointer with the low bit reserved as a waiter-present flag; locked testing checks for non-null owner while owner extraction masks off the flag, both performed as racy reads.

Construction helpers include a runtime initializer binding caller context and a static class, a static initializer and defining macro, a no-op task-free hook, and lock macros for plain, subclass-nested and nest-lock forms whose availability depends on configuration.

Reader-writer lock facade offers shared and exclusive lock, unlock and trylock plus interrupt-saving, interrupt-disabling and bottom-half variants with matching unlocks, a nested exclusive form, a write trylock combining interrupt save, and a contention query.

Multiprocessor wrappers hold preemption off across acquisition, record dependence before attempting the architecture primitive, retry through a contention helper on failure, extend the hold across interrupt or bottom-half masking for the corresponding variants, and on release record dependence release before delegating to the architecture primitive and restoring prior state; try forms undo the hold when the primitive refuses.

Uniprocessor architecture try operations unconditionally report success after a compiler barrier while ignoring the lock argument, and contention reporting either queries the architecture primitive or constantly reports idle.

Reference count lifecycle moves among positive owned, zero released and saturated error conditions: conditional raises stay in positive or fail at zero, unconditional raises from zero or any wrap into negativity moves to saturated error, and a subtract that exactly consumes the remaining positive balance moves to zero with success while any overshoot moves to saturated error.

Per-CPU semaphore readers occupy either a fast biased condition using per-CPU counters while the synchronizer stays idle or a slow condition delegating to shared helpers once the synchronizer leaves idle; writers use a block indicator to force new readers into the slow condition and later restore idle to resume fast bias.

Callable entry points covered here include per-CPU shared acquire and release, reference count read and update helpers, real-time mutex lock forms, and reader-writer shared and exclusive lock and unlock operations across normal, interrupt and bottom-half contexts.

Reader-writer initialization either binds a static lock class with name and key through a helper or directly assigns an unlocked value, selected by configuration, ensuring defined dependence state before first use.
All inspection and mutation of the real-time waiter tree and owner is serialized by the embedded raw spin wait lock, with annotations marking the guarded fields.
